expected:
The public-source-hygiene contract is order-independent: no test in the
suite leaves a `__pycache__` under `dadaia_workspace/public/scripts/`. The standalone
script `generate-memory-catalog.py` sets `sys.dont_write_bytecode = True` (line 60), but
a test that imports it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(...)` (e.g.
`tests/integration/scripts/test_generate_memory_catalog.py:40`) — or another importer in
the full-run ordering — can cause CPython to write the module's own bytecode *before* the
in-module guard line executes, polluting `public/scripts/`.

**Notes / scope:**
- **Pre-existing, NOT introduced by release v0.1.18.** The three involved files
  (`public/scripts/generate-memory-catalog.py`,
  `tests/integration/scripts/test_generate_memory_catalog.py`,
  `tests/contract/test_public_source_hygiene.py`) are byte-identical to the release base
  `f980cd7` (`git diff f980cd7..97cd5f6 -- <those> | wc -l` = 0). The v0.1.18 NEW tests
  (`test_catalog.py`, `test_lint_memory_atoms.py`) do NOT pollute `public/scripts/` when
  run in isolation (verified clean).
- The polluting artifact is **untracked / gitignored** — never committed, never in any
  release diff. It is purely a working-tree/CI-run pollution.
- **Impact on the push gate:** the pre-push `dadaia ci preflight` runs the full suite, so
  this flake can intermittently RED the push gate for any release. Recommend fixing before
  the v0.1.18 push (rc boundary), not as an alpha-gate blocker.
- **Suggested fixes:** (a) make `test_generate_memory_catalog.py` (and any other importer
  of a `public/scripts/*.py`) import under `sys.dont_write_bytecode = True` set in the test
  module *before* the `spec_from_file_location` exec, or run the script only via
  `subprocess … -B`; and/or (b) add a session-scoped autouse fixture that asserts/cleans
  `public/**/__pycache__` so the hygiene contract is deterministic regardless of ordering;
  and/or (c) move the bytecode guard to the script's `#!`/`-B` invocation contract and have
  the contract test tolerate a transient cache it cleans in teardown.
- Found during the v0.1.18 (`pi-operational-two-layer`) alpha QA gate, 2026-06-25.
repro:
1. From a clean working tree (`rm -rf dadaia_workspace/public/scripts/__pycache__`), run
   the full suite: `.dadaia/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q`.
2. Observe the two `test_public_source_hygiene.py` failures.
3. Run the contract module alone on a clean tree
   (`pytest tests/contract/test_public_source_hygiene.py`) → 3 passed (no failure).
4. Running subsets (`tests/integration/scripts/ tests/unit/scripts/
   tests/contract/test_public_source_hygiene.py`) also pass — the pollution only
   manifests in the full-suite ordering.
symptom:
In a full `pytest` run of the whole suite, two contract tests in
`tests/contract/test_public_source_hygiene.py` FAIL:

- `test_no_bytecode_committed_under_public`
- `test_running_public_scripts_leaves_no_pycache`

Both fail because `dadaia_workspace/public/scripts/__pycache__/generate-memory-catalog.cpython-312.pyc`
exists at the time the contract test runs. Observed run:
`2 failed, 3348 passed, 11 skipped in 249.41s`.
title: public-source-hygiene-flaky-pycache-pollution

component: dadaia release new (release-id validator) vs dadaia specs doctor (SPEC-DOC-027 naming canon)
expected:
One coherent naming contract. Either (a) `release new` accepts the SemVer
`v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>` form the doctor canon mandates, or (b) the doctor canon recognises
the documented descriptive-slug convention the CLI actually produces (e.g. an allowlisted
`<slug>-vN` pattern for live dirs, not only the `_archive` legacy allowlist).

**Notes / impact (not blocking this release):**
- The error is NOT CI-gated (no `specs doctor` job in CI) and downgrades to a WARNING once the
  release dir is archived (`is_live=False`), so every session release dodged it by being
  doctored only post-archive. The live-phase ERROR is therefore transient but real.
- Accumulating effect: archived slug dirs that are not on the `_archive` legacy allowlist
  (`RELEASE_NAMING_LEGACY_ALLOWLIST`) remain permanent SPEC-DOC-027 **WARNINGs** — slow drift
  the operator should resolve with a naming-policy decision (rename history, extend the
  allowlist convention, or fix `release new` to mint SemVer).
- Root-cause fix belongs in a release-tooling release, not in `pi-operational-two-layer-v1`
  (scope = make PI operational). Filed here for the operator/project-manager to schedule.
repro:
1. `dadaia release new v0.1.18 …` → rejected (dot in id).
2. Create the release as a slug instead (e.g. `pi-operational-two-layer-v1`), SPEC `Created:`
   ≥ 2026-06-01, leave it live in `specs/releases/`.
3. `dadaia specs doctor --specs-dir specs` → `[ERR] SPEC-DOC-027: Release dir … does not
   follow the naming canon ^v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>$ — rename it`.
symptom:
Two tooling rules give contradictory naming constraints for a release directory:
- `dadaia release new <id>` rejects any id containing a dot — the id validator is
  `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$` (no dots), so `v0.1.16` is refused at creation time.
- `dadaia specs doctor` SPEC-DOC-027 (`features/specs/doctor.py:1177`) REQUIRES a release
  dir to match `^v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>$` (dots mandatory) and emits an **ERROR** for a
  non-conforming dir that is **live in `specs/releases/`** with a SPEC `Created:` date on/after
  `RELEASE_SEMVER_CUTOFF` (2026-06-01).

There is no name that satisfies both: SemVer is blocked at creation, descriptive slugs are
flagged by the doctor. This forced a slug workaround for every recent release
(`multiharness-engine-v0116`, `pi-fourth-harness-v1`, `pi-operational-two-layer-v1`).
title: release-new-rejects-semver-but-doctor-requires-it

expected:
The two doctors should agree on the terminal-status vocabulary for a
consumed/shipped backlog item — one canonical format that passes BL-SCHEMA and
silences SPEC-DOC-031. Options: (a) BL-SCHEMA parses `TOKEN — vX.Y.Z` by splitting
on the em-dash and validating the leading token (accepting the version suffix); or
(b) SPEC-DOC-031 accepts a bare terminal token plus a separate `delivered_in:` /
evidence frontmatter field instead of demanding the suffix inside `status:`.

**Workaround applied (v0.1.26 closure):** set `status: delivered` + a separate
`delivered_in: v0.1.26` frontmatter field on the consumed epic. BL-SCHEMA passes;
SPEC-DOC-031 remains a non-blocking WARN (same advisory class already present on
~7 other archived-referenced candidate items).
repro:
1. Set a backlog item's `status: DELIVERED — v0.1.26`.
2. `git commit` anything → pre-commit `backlog doctor` BL-SCHEMA ERROR (blocks).
3. Set `status: delivered` → commit passes, but `dadaia specs doctor` emits
   SPEC-DOC-031 WARN asking for the `TOKEN — vX.Y.Z` form.
symptom:
A consumed/shipped backlog item cannot satisfy both backlog-status
checks at once. `backlog doctor` BL-SCHEMA validates `status.lower()` against a set
of **bare** tokens (`_KNOWN_STATUSES = {idea, candidate, picked, in-progress,
delivered, rejected, deferred, done, closed, open}`) and HARD-ERRORs anything else.
`specs doctor` SPEC-DOC-031 instead asks a consumed item to use a terminal token
**with a version suffix**: `DELIVERED — vX.Y.Z` (also SUPERSEDED/RESOLVED/CONSUMED).
Setting `status: DELIVERED — v0.1.26` (the SPEC-DOC-031 form) makes
`"delivered — v0.1.26"` ∉ `_KNOWN_STATUSES`, so BL-SCHEMA blocks the commit:

```
[pre-commit] BLOCKED: backlog doctor found 1 error(s):
  BL-SCHEMA [backlog-definition-workflow-dedup-conflict-control] invalid status 'DELIVERED — v0.1.26'
```

Conversely, the BL-SCHEMA-valid bare `delivered` leaves a SPEC-DOC-031 WARN (it
wants the version + evidence pointer). No single `status:` value satisfies both
enforcement points.
title: backlog-doctor-bl-schema-vs-spec-doc-031-terminal-status-format-conflict

'panel:/api/workflow-model-policy' (kind=api) has no alias-map entry; panel/api

component: features/panel (index.py inline mermaid script + CSP) / tests/e2e/panel (ops-tab OPS-02) / ci preflight scope
expected:
A pushed branch that passes the pre-push gate should also pass the
GitHub Actions panel-e2e job. The panel must serve no CSP-violating inline
script, and E2E assertions must track the live panel layout.

**Process gap (the reason this reached `main`-bound CI red):** the pre-push CI
gate / `dadaia ci preflight` runs only `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`,
`mypy --strict`, and `pytest` — it does **not** run the Playwright panel E2E
suite. So a panel regression passes the local preflight and the pre-push gate and
is only caught by the GitHub Actions `E2E panel (Playwright)` job after the push.
Closure (qa+security APPROVE) likewise did not run the panel E2E job. Consider
either (a) adding a panel-e2e step to `dadaia ci preflight` (gated on node/browser
availability), or (b) documenting that panel E2E is CI-only and must be run by qa
before any release that touches `features/panel/`.

**Fix applied (this session):**
- Removed the dead inline `<script type="module">` mermaid-hydration block from
  `index.py` (kept the server-rendered SVG DAG and the `<pre class="mermaid">`
  raw-source block, which matches the memory-atom rendering convention). No CSP
  hash added — the script is gone, not allowlisted.
- Updated `tests/e2e/panel/ops-tab.spec.ts` OPS-02 to assert the 4-subsection
  order `agents → workflows → dadaia-workflows → kanban`.
- Verified: full local panel E2E suite 61/61 green; `dadaia ci preflight` PASS.
repro:
```
cd repos/dadaia-workspace/tests/e2e/panel
PANEL_WEB_SERVER_COMMAND="<ws>/.dadaia/.venv/bin/python -m dadaia_workspace.cli.main panel --port 4999 --no-open" \
  npx playwright test ops-tab.spec.ts response-guard.spec.ts servers-tab.spec.ts tab-navigation.spec.ts
# pre-fix: 5 failures (OPS-02 mismatch + 4 CSP console errors)
```
symptom:
The GitHub Actions "E2E panel (Playwright)" job failed on
`feature/v0.1.25` (run 28246442927) with 5 failing tests, all from two root
causes shipped in v0.1.24 and missed at closure:

1. **CSP violation (4 tests):** OPS-06, E2E-GUARD-02, E2E-SRV-01, E2E-TAB-04 each
   reported exactly one console error:
   `Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy
   directive 'script-src 'self' 'sha256-GRTndW6m…' 'sha256-u9QKVWf5…''. …
   a hash ('sha256-5YRJUPM6Z2462aK6lDuJhdzswItM+S6oQ+jQQelGOOI=') … is required.
   The action has been blocked.`
   The blocked hash is the inline `<script type="module">` mermaid-hydration
   block in `dadaia_workspace/features/panel/views/index.py` (added in v0.1.24
   cba8c22 for the dadaia-workflows catalog). Its sha256 was never added to the
   panel CSP allowlist (`_CSP_SCRIPT_HASH_*` in `handler.py`). Worse, the script
   is **doubly dead**: even if allowlisted, it does `import('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/…mermaid…')`,
   and the panel CSP `script-src` is `'self'` + hashed inline only — it does not
   permit any external CDN origin, so the import can never execute. The panel is
   loopback/offline by design and already renders a server-rendered SVG DAG per
   workflow; client-side mermaid hydration is fundamentally incompatible with the
   panel's security posture and its existing no-CDN/no-mermaid invariant tests
   (E2E-TAB-06, workflows-tab "does not load Mermaid").

2. **Stale E2E assertion (1 test):** OPS-02 asserted the Ops sub-section at index
   2 is `ops-subsection-kanban`, but v0.1.24 inserted `ops-subsection-dadaia-workflows`
   between `workflows` and `kanban`, making the live order
   `agents → workflows → dadaia-workflows → kanban`. The test was not updated.
title: panel-csp-blocks-mermaid-cdn-script-and-stale-ops-subsection-test

3. The same suite is **green on GitHub Actions runners** (every prior release shipped

repro:
run the v0.1.31 real-worker e2e against the strict (pre-hardening) extractor:
```

  .dadaia/.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/integration/pi_live/test_real_layer2_worker_workflow_e2e.py
# pre-hardening: BLOCKED release_scope "agent result missing artifact evidence"
```

**Expected / fix direction:** disambiguate the prompt so the worker is told exactly ONE
`schema` value to emit, and make `expected_schema` per-step consistent with what the envelope
instructs. Either (a) thread the fragment's `output_schema` through as the single
`expected_schema` and instruct the worker to put *that* in the `schema` field; or (b) keep
`agent-run-result-v1` as the transport and stop surfacing the fragment `output_schema` as a
second "schema" to emit (carry it only as an internal field). Then the strict equality check
can be restored and the structural-tolerance fallback in `_verdict_payload` becomes
defence-in-depth rather than the primary path.
symptom:
A real `pi`/Codex Layer-2 worker is told to emit its step result against **two
different schema names** and labels the result inconsistently across runs, so a strict
`schema`-field equality check drops a correct payload. Observed live on `release_scope`
(gpt-5.5), two consecutive runs:
- run 1: top-level `"schema": "agent-run-result-v1"` (the transport schema — matched);
- run 2: NO top-level `schema`; instead `"output_schema": "release-scope-handoff-v1"` nested
  inside `structured_output` (the fragment's domain schema — did NOT match).

Both payloads were otherwise correct (non-empty `artifact_refs`, `status`, `verdict`).

**Root cause:** the prompt presents two schema identifiers:
- `prompt_builder.PromptScope.expected_schema` defaults to `"agent-run-result-v1"` (the
  transport/result-object schema the extractor checks); and
- the per-step fragment declares its own `output_schema` (e.g. `release-scope-handoff-v1`),
  which the envelope text also surfaces to the worker
  (`prompt_builder.py:~72` "conforms to the output schema `{bundle.output_schema}`").
The worker sees both and can't reliably decide which to put in the `schema` field. The
extractor (`_verdict_payload`) historically required `payload["schema"] == expected_schema`
exactly, so a domain-schema-labelled (or unlabelled) result was silently dropped → the step
BLOCKed with "agent result missing artifact evidence".

component: panel workflow model-governance editor (workflow_policy.py / workflow_model_policy overlay / policy_resolver)
expected: see archived source specs/bugs/_archive/v0145-t4506-kimi-raw-model-cannot-persist-via-profile-overlay.md
repro:
```
.dadaia/.venv/bin/python -c "
from dadaia_workspace.features.workflows.dadaia_catalog import governed_workflow_catalog
from dadaia_workspace.features.lifecycle.policy_resolver import (
    WorkflowExecutionPolicyResolver, StepOverride)
r = WorkflowExecutionPolicyResolver(catalog=governed_workflow_catalog())
r.resolve('implementation', cli_overrides=(StepOverride(step='implement', profile_id='kimi-2.7:high'),))
"
# -> PolicyResolutionError: unknown model profile 'kimi-2.7:high'; valid profiles:
#    codex-implementation-standard, codex-review-deep, pi-implementation-standard,
#    pi-reasoning-high, pi-reasoning-low
```

**Root cause (architecture mismatch, arch finding #3 vs the shipped overlay):**
- The panel editor + overlay store + resolver persist a **profile id** per step
  (`WorkflowModelPolicyOverlay.contexts[ctx].workflows[wf].steps[step] = <profile_id>`),
  validated against the built-in `model_profiles` registry.
- `model_profiles` has **no kimi profile** — v0.1.44 added `kimi-2.7` to the *allowed
  concrete-model set* (`harness_models.LAYER2_EXTRA_MODEL_IDS` / `known_layer2_model_ids()`)
  but did **not** add a governed profile that resolves to it.
- Therefore a step override of the raw model id `kimi-2.7:high` is rejected by the
  resolver, and `validate`-before-`save` blocks the PUT. Even if a kimi profile were
  added, the **persisted** overlay value would be the *profile id*, never the literal
  `kimi-2.7:high`, so the T-45-06 round-trip assertion (persisted value ==
  `kimi-2.7:high`) still could not hold.

**Expected (per T-45-06 / SPEC AC-3):** selecting the OpenRouter kimi option persists
`kimi-2.7:high` verbatim and the resolver honours it — with **no changes to
`core/harness_models.py` allowed-set logic, the overlay store, or the resolver** (T-45-06
constraint) and **no new model-governance semantics** (SPEC §4). These constraints are
mutually exclusive with the requirement: a raw-model overlay would require changing the

Root cause: the bind-driven injection step selects the newest bind-epoch marker newer than this session's sentinel across ALL contexts — markers carry a slug but no session affinity, so with concurrent sessions in different contexts the most recent bind wins for every session whose sentinel is older. The flagship parallel-multi-project scenario is exactly the one that breaks; the wrong project's memory can steer wrong-project writes.

component: dadaia lifecycle release-definition --harness codex (live review rejection) | features/lifecycle/workflows/_fragment_gate.py review-rejection return
expected: A rejected-review block must prescribe the exact recovery: re-run the same run id with --resume-from <the create step the review consumes> and the run's own harness, so the operator can address the findings and continue. No gate block is a dead end.
repro: Run release-definition with a live worker until a review REJECTS twice (budget spent), then read blocked.operator_command -> null
symptom: On the live path, plan_review REJECTED the PLAN for a substantive reason and the run blocked with operator_command: null. The validator reported it could not proceed 'without inventing a change', which is exactly right: the operator is handed a rejection and no prescribed way forward. The workflow spends one bounded in-run revision of the create step and then returns the reviewer's RAW block unenriched, so the block carries whatever the reviewer produced — and a reviewer never fills operator_command. Every other gate in the engine prescribes its recovery; this one, the one a real release hits most often, does not.
title: A rejected review with the revision budget spent blocks with operator_command null — a dead end

component: dadaia lifecycle <workflow> --run-id <blocked run> (no --resume-from) | features/lifecycle run start path
expected: A BLOCKED run must not silently restart. Refuse it the way a COMPLETED re-run is refused, naming the recorded remedy and offering the two real choices: resume with --resume-from, or pass a fresh --run-id to start over deliberately.
repro: Block a run, note blocked.operator_command, then re-run the identical command with the same --run-id and no --resume-from; the block is replaced by a fresh one from step 1
symptom: Re-invoking a workflow with the run id of a run that is BLOCKED, without --resume-from, does not resume and does not refuse: it starts the sequence over from the first step. The recorded block - its reason, its findings, and the operator_command that prescribes the recovery - is erased. Reproduced deterministically: a backlog-definition run blocked at backlog_review_gate with a remedy; re-running the identical command moved the block to backlog_author, destroying the original diagnosis. The consumer-side validator hit this on a LIVE release: the plan_review block vanished and the run restarted at spec_create. Re-running the same command is the most natural thing an operator does after a block, and it costs them the very information they need - and, on a live run, real worker spend.
title: Re-running a BLOCKED run with the same run id silently restarts it and destroys the block and its remedy

component: dadaia lifecycle release-definition --harness codex (driver interrupted) | features/lifecycle run start path

symptom: Interrupting release-definition leaves the Codex worker orphaned and the run persisted as 'running' at its current step: not finished, not failed, carrying no block and therefore no operator_command. The operator is left with a run that offers no guidance, and re-running the same command silently restarts from step one - redoing accepted live work at real cost.
title: An interrupted run is left RUNNING with no terminal state and no remedy

component: dadaia lifecycle release-definition --harness codex --resume-from plan_create (live) | features/lifecycle/workflows/_fragment_gate.py resume + in-run revision payload attempts
expected: A re-executed create step must write a NEW attempt rather than mutating the attempt whose hash the ledger already recorded; and any handoff-immutability block must carry an operator_command, since no gate block may be a dead end.
repro: Start a live release-definition, interrupt it after spec_review, resume with --resume-from plan_create, let plan_create+plan_review complete, and watch tasks_create block on the plan_create attempt-0 hash mismatch
symptom: Resuming a live release from plan_create advanced correctly through plan_create and plan_review, then BLOCKED at tasks_create with: 'required upstream handoff unavailable: step payload content hash mismatch for .../handoffs/r11-release-1/steps/plan_create-attempt-0.step-payload.json (payload was mutated - immutability violated)'. The ledger records spec_create, spec_review, plan_create, plan_review as accepted, so the work was done; the run still cannot advance because the plan_create payload on disk no longer hashes to what the ledger recorded. The block carries operator_command: null - another dead end, on the same run that the interrupted-run and rejected-review remedies were just added for. This is the release-definition-retry-collides-with-immutable-tasks-payload class resurfacing at a different step: a re-executed create step (resume, or the bounded in-run revision after a review rejection) writes over attempt-0 instead of recording a new attempt, so the immutable payload it already registered is mutated underneath the ledger.
title: A resumed create step rewrites attempt-0's payload, so the next step dies on an immutability violation with no remedy

component: dadaia lifecycle release-definition --resume-from <create step> (live) | cli/commands/lifecycle.py release_define options
expected: release-definition accepts --demand exactly as backlog-definition does, injected into every executed model step's prompt, so an operator resuming after a rejection can supply the missing decision instead of re-rolling the same dice.
repro: dadaia lifecycle release-definition --context <c> --release-id <r> --run-id <id> --harness codex --resume-from tasks_create --demand 'do X' -> 'No such option: --demand'
symptom: backlog-definition accepts --demand, which injects an '## Operator demand' block into every model step's prompt. release-definition does NOT: 'No such option: --demand'. So when a review REJECTS a SPEC, PLAN or TASKS, the operator's only channel back into the next attempt is the rejection digest the engine injects automatically - they cannot add the specific correction, constraint or decision the reviewer asked for. Observed on the live path across three rejection cycles of one release: the reviewer moved from a pytest cache-flag lint, to unresolved toolchain markers, to 'the draft leaves essential construction, serialization and storage-mapping decisions to the implementer'. The model IS converging, but each cycle costs minutes of live worker time and the operator has to sit and hope rather than say the one sentence that would resolve it.
title: release-definition has no --demand, so an operator cannot inject the correction a review asked for

repro: Run release-definition live; when tasks_implementability_review rejects repeatedly for unspecified implementation decisions, read the approved PLAN and check whether it carries exact signatures, field types and module paths for each caller-facing surface
symptom: This is the ROOT CAUSE of tasks-implementability-review-does-not-converge-on-a-real-release, found by diffing the three fragments against each other. plan-create.md REQUIRES, for every new or changed caller-facing surface, an explicit contract binding - exact public type/function/method names, parameter and return signatures, field names/types, module/export path - and says in as many words 'do not leave them for TASKS or implementation to invent'. tasks-create.md then FORBIDS the author from supplying what the PLAN omitted: it must copy the bindings 'already approved in the PLAN' and 'never invent a binding missing from the approved PLAN'. tasks-review-implementability.md REQUIRES those same bindings to be present. So when plan_review approves a PLAN that lacks them, the TASKS author is trapped between two rules it cannot both satisfy, and the rejection lands at tasks_implementability_review - one step downstream of where the omission actually happened, and at the one step that cannot repair it. title: plan_review approves a PLAN without contract bindings, trapping tasks_create in an unsatisfiable gate

symptom: After PR #200 squash-merged to main, the reconciliation merge on develop publishes ZERO blobs and TWO commit objects; the range-scoped scan reads commit BODIES (v0.4.3 hardening) and refuses main's squash commit body at line 1160 on baseline pattern 'home-abs-path'. The matched value is a SYNTHETIC test-fixture literal (/home/[REDACTED] an obviously non-operator placeholder quoted in a commit subject describing the substring-amnesty repro), so it is a true positive against the pattern but a false positive in privacy terms. The refusal message states 'the range scope means already-published history never needs a rewrite' and prescribes --amend / interactive rebase / cherry-pick, but the offending object IS already published (git branch -r --contains -> origin/main) and is GitHub-authored; amending it would rewrite published main history and destroy the tree/lineage identity the reconciliation merge exists to record. title: Push-range body scan refuses a reconciliation merge over main's already-published squash commit, whose prescribed remedy (amend) is inapplicable

Run 'dadaia specs upgrade --specs-dir <tree> --dry-run' — it plans agent-tier-frontmatter moves and reports no problem. 3. Run it for real with -y. 4. The step rewrites the atoms and the post-upgrade doctor reports new LINT-1 errors; the command exits fail and points at its backup.
symptom: Upgrading a consumer specs tree from pattern version 0/1 to the canonical 4 runs the agent-tier-frontmatter step over specs/memory/*.md and then fails its own post-check: 'upgrade introduced 1 new doctor error(s)' — LINT-1, 'Frontmatter schema violation: Additional properties are not allowed (token_estimate was unexpected)' on architecture.md, quality-assurance.md and tech-stack.md. title: specs upgrade rewrites memory atoms into frontmatter the shipped schema rejects (token_estimate)

expected: An error present before the migration stays classified as pre-existing regardless of how many other atoms the migration repaired - the fail-and-restore path is reserved for regressions the migration itself introduced. Comparison should be per-atom/per-finding identity rather than the aggregated description string.
repro: 1. Scaffold a specs tree, regress its constitution stamp to pattern version 1, and give three memory atoms the retired keys agent_tier and token_estimate. 2. Add a fourth atom as a SYMLINK whose target lives outside the specs tree and also carries a retired key. 3. Run 'dadaia specs upgrade --specs-dir <tree> -y'. Observed: the three real atoms migrate, the symlinked one is correctly refused by the link guard, and the command exits 1 with 'upgrade introduced 1 new doctor error(s). Restore from: <backup>' naming the symlinked atom. Control: repeat with the symlinked atom as the ONLY violator (no other retired keys anywhere) and the same tree reports '[warn] ... 1 pre-existing doctor error(s) remain (not caused by the upgrade) - fix separately, do NOT restore' and exits 0. The only difference is whether the aggregated description changed.
symptom: The pre/post doctor comparison keys on the tuple (code, description), but LINT-1 aggregates EVERY violating memory atom into one issue whose description lists them all. When a migration fixes some violating atoms and legitimately skips another (a symlinked atom under the new link-refusal guard, or an unreadable/unwritable one under the new skip paths), the LINT-1 description shrinks, no longer matches the pre-migration snapshot, and the residual violation is misclassified as newly introduced. The command then prints 'upgrade introduced 1 new doctor error(s). Restore from: <backup>' and exits 1 even though the tree reached the target pattern version cleanly and the surviving violation predates the run. Following that instruction discards a good version bump while leaving the same error in place - exactly the harm the code's own comment says the comparison exists to prevent.

expected: A fixture aged for a test that injects a clock is aged by THAT clock, so the test asserts the same thing on every calendar day. A test whose result depends on the wall-clock date is a time bomb, not a test.
repro: 1. Run the tmp_gc suite while the real UTC date equals 2026-08-18 — green. 2. Run the identical commit after 00:00Z on 2026-08-19 — four tests fail on marker-age assertions. No code change in between.
symptom: run_tmp_gc takes an injectable now and the tests pass a frozen _NOW = 2026-08-18T00:00Z, but the fixture helpers age files with time.time() (the real clock): _write_marker at line 49, and raw os.utime aging at lines 109 and 318. The service therefore measures a real-clock mtime against a frozen now, so the effective age drifts by exactly the distance between the two. A marker written as '4 days old' had only about 0.04 days of margin over the 3-day threshold. When real UTC crossed midnight into 2026-08-19 the age fell to 2.99 days and four tests began failing: test_orphan_marker_older_than_three_days_reaped, test_dry_run_reports_all_lanes_without_deleting_anything, test_idempotent_second_real_run_is_a_pure_no_op, test_unlink_failure_is_best_effort_and_does_not_abort_other_lanes. The same suite passed 30 minutes earlier on the same commit and the same machine; CI went red on Linux, macOS and Windows simultaneously.
title: tmp_gc tests age fixtures with the real clock while injecting a frozen now — the suite breaks at a UTC date boundary

cause: shared git index between two sessions in one checkout is a git contract, not a library contract; practice = one session per checkout/worktree (ADR 0002, accepted); revisit only if a harness gains a per-session cwd
component: shared working-tree git index (no locking between concurrent agent Bash tool sessions)
expected: Commit-shape isolation (dd-gitflow-default section 3a, D10) assumes each agent's stage-then-commit sequence is atomic and produces the message the task specifies. No lock or advisory mechanism protects the shared git index across concurrent Bash-tool sessions in the same working tree, unlike the SDD file-write gate which does surface presence advisories.
repro: Two agent sessions with Bash tool access operate in the same working tree concurrently. Session A: git add fileX fileY (no commit yet). Session B: git add -A && git commit -m '...'. Session A's git status --porcelain now shows fileX/fileY already committed under session B's sha, not session A's intended message.
symptom: Agent A staged exactly two files (git add path1 path2) for an isolated task commit. Before Agent A ran git commit, a concurrent Agent B ran git add -A (or similar) + git commit for its own unrelated change; Agent B's commit included Agent A's already-staged files, landing them under Agent B's commit message instead of Agent A's intended isolated-commit-shape message.
title: Concurrent Bash-tool agent sessions share one git index; one session's git add can be swept into another session's unrelated git commit

cause: core/release_events.py:113 used text.splitlines() to split RELEASE.jsonl into physical lines instead of text.split(chr(10)); splitlines() treats U+2028/U+2029/U+0085/U+000B/U+000C as line terminators too, so a literal one of these characters embedded in a note's free-text field fragments one physical JSONL line into two invalid JSON fragments.

expected: A note event carrying a literal U+2028 (or U+2029/U+0085/U+000B/U+000C) inside its data.text field folds to exactly one ReleaseEvent, with zero parse errors -- the reader splits on a literal newline character only, never str.splitlines()'s wider terminator set, matching every other JSONL reader in this release.
repro: Write one RELEASE.jsonl line whose note.data.text contains a literal U+2028 character, then call parse_release_events(text): the fold reports two parse errors and zero events for that line instead of one note event.
solution: Changed parse_release_events to split on text.split(chr(10)) only, matching the fix already carried at jsonl_record_store.py, migrate_v5.py and doctor_governance.py; RED-then-GREEN regression test tests/unit/core/test_release_events.py::test_a_note_carrying_a_unicode_line_separator_folds_to_one_event_not_zero (S1-FR23-firing.md amendment A4).
symptom: parse_release_events splits RELEASE.jsonl text with text.splitlines(), which treats U+2028/U+2029/U+0085/U+000B/U+000C as line terminators; a note event whose data.text field embeds one of these characters fragments the physical JSONL line into two halves that both fail json.loads, so the event is silently dropped and recorded only as two parse errors.

cause: the store's own re-read-and-compare staleness check ran in the CALLER (JsonlRecordStore.update/remove) before invoking the separate, unconditional atomic_write() call, leaving a gap for the whole duration atomic_write spent serializing content to its temp sibling; a concurrent session's real O_APPEND append landing in that gap was invisible to the already-passed check and got silently discarded by the swap that followed, with the losing update commands still exiting 0
evidence_diff: net-positive: production +69/-18 LOC across core/atomic_write.py (+49/-4, new ConcurrentModificationError plus expected_previous CAS param on the sole existing temp-then-replace primitive, proven by tests/unit/core/test_atomic_write_census.py) and infrastructure/jsonl_record_store.py (+20/-14, dropped its own duplicated re-read-then-write in favour of the primitive's new check) -- net LOC rose because a genuine new correctness capability was missing from the primitive; routes to software-architect per the standing architecture-review order
evidence_loop: pytest tests/unit/infrastructure/test_jsonl_record_store.py::test_update_refuses_a_concurrent_append_that_lands_after_the_rereads_own_check -> DID NOT RAISE StaleRecordWriteError at HEAD before the fix (concurrent append silently discarded)
expected: Either the append re-reads the ledger immediately before writing so concurrent updates survive, or it refuses stale and exits non-zero naming the re-read-and-retry remedy, as the seam's own contract states. A silent whole-file overwrite that discards committed governance writes is the loss the atomic-write seam exists to prevent.
repro: 1. In session A, run 'dadaia bugs update <id> --set audited=<slug>' across many records. 2. In session B, while A is running or shortly after, run 'dadaia bugs append --bug-id <new>'. 3. Read the ledger: session B's record is present and session A's updates are absent. 4. Note that every command in both sessions exited 0.
solution: atomic_write() gained an optional expected_previous CAS parameter, re-read as its LAST step immediately before os.replace, raising core.atomic_write.ConcurrentModificationError (translated to StaleRecordWriteError) instead of swapping; update()/remove() now pass expected_previous=<their own snapshot> instead of performing their own separate re-read-then-write
symptom: An audit wrote the audited field plus derived provenance on 507 records, one atomic update per record through the AS-16 seam; all 507 exited 0 with '[ok] updated'. A concurrent session then ran 'bugs append' for a new record. After that append the ledger contained the new record and NONE of the 507 updates: every audited field was null again. No update reported a stale-read refusal, and the append reported success, so the loss is silent on both sides. The seam documents itself as atomic with a re-read before write and a refuse-stale exit; a whole-file write built from a snapshot taken before the concurrent updates is neither.
title: a concurrent bugs append silently discards another session's completed update batch — 507 governance writes lost with every update exiting 0

cause: log_added_lines walked git log --all --no-merges --reverse --date-order with no --full-history flag; git's default treesame-based history simplification, at every merge whose tree for the pathspec exactly matched one parent, followed only that parent and never queued the other parent for traversal at all -- silently dropping any commit reachable only through that pruned parent (routinely a deleted post-merge feature branch, the exact shape dd-gitflow-default mandates). F030 (ADR-0016's contract re-derives with the same walk so it cannot fail) is closed by this same fix: the contract was re-deriving through the identically under-reporting walk, so it could never catch this class of drift -- it now walks the corrected history.
evidence_diff: net-neutral: production +16/-4 LOC in infrastructure/git_subprocess.py, almost entirely a docstring explaining why --full-history is load-bearing -- the functional change is a single flag added to an existing git log invocation, no new parameter, no new branch, no new code path
evidence_loop: pytest tests/contract/test_git_history_reader_log_added_lines.py::test_log_added_lines_sees_a_commit_history_simplification_would_otherwise_hide -> AssertionError: t1 (the commit history simplification hides without --full-history) is missing from the walk, at HEAD before the fix
expected: log_added_lines includes --full-history in its git log invocation so every commit that ever touched the pathspec is walked, regardless of whether a later merge's simplification would otherwise treesame-prune it away; ADR-0016 (stored provenance equals derived provenance) cannot be honestly satisfied by a derivation that structurally under-reports its own source history.
repro: In a synthetic repo: commit A0 creates specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl; branch topic off A0 and commit T1 appends a line to it; on the original branch commit A1 touches an unrelated file; build a merge commit M with parents [A1, T1] whose tree for BUGS.jsonl is byte-identical to A1's (T1's change is discarded by the merge resolution); delete the topic ref. Run 'git log --all --no-merges --reverse --date-order -- specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl': T1 is absent. Re-run with --full-history added: T1 appears.
solution: added --full-history to the git log invocation in GitSubprocessClient.log_added_lines
symptom: log_added_lines walks 'git log --all --no-merges --reverse --date-order -- specs/bugs/' with no --full-history flag. Git's default history simplification prunes a commit that touched the pathspec on a branch whose later merge discarded that change and whose ref was since deleted (a routine gitflow shape: feature branch merged then deleted) -- the commit becomes unreachable via the simplified walk even though it is still a real ancestor. The security verdict naming develop's pre-merge tip is committed on the feature branch BEFORE the final feature->develop merge, so it rides into develop and the post-merge develop tip's first parent equals that named sha — the SAME first-parent branch covering_verdict already has. skill dd-gitflow-default carries the protocol text (authored by another concurrent session). evidence_loop: pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/unit/test_spec_context_doctor_root.py tests/contract/cli/test_doctor_scan_cli.py -k undeletable — RED before the fix: PermissionError [Errno 13] escaped fix(); the CliRunner result.exception was the OSError

Exit code reflects remaining findings, never a traceback. The SessionStart hook run must never fail on an undeletable file.
repro: 1. Fresh workspace: dadaia init --workspace <dir>. 2. mkdir -p <dir>/.dadaia/tmp/x/deps; touch <dir>/.dadaia/tmp/x/deps/a.js; touch <dir>/.dadaia/tmp/x/other.txt; set both 2 days old via os.utime; chmod 555 <dir>/.dadaia/tmp/x/deps (or make it root-owned). 3. dadaia doctor  -> lists WS-tmp-expired for both files. 4. dadaia doctor --fix  -> Error: unexpected PermissionError, exit 1, 'Applied' block absent; other.txt still present although it was deletable. 5. dadaia doctor --fix --expired-only --quiet -> same crash.
solution: _delete wraps the single _remove call site: an OSError becomes a "<code>: skipped '<path>' (errno N: reason)" action, the pass continues to every other entry, and the returned actions name exactly what was deleted.
